reason: Portal and desktop each own one lazy application catalogue source and persisted language controls; native desktop locale persistence is isolated behind the existing trusted IPC boundary. The two shared UI libraries export independent CatalogueSources instead of duplicating their messages into every app. Small build-time macro/catalogue transforms replace uncompiled macros in published JS. One permission-label helper is reused by both consent screens to avoid untranslatable verb fragments. This adds no remote service, collection protocol, workspace package or authorization state.
